title: Understanding Bootstrapping
text: Bootstrapping is a statistical method that involves resampling with replacement from a dataset to create many simulated samples. This technique is often used to estimate the sampling distribution of a statistic.

title: Why Use Bootstrapping?
text: Bootstrapping is useful when the theoretical distribution of a statistic is complex or unknown. It allows us to approximate the distribution by using the data itself.

title: Sample Size Consideration
text: The sample size of $$500$$ trips on May $$1$$ is relatively large, which is beneficial for bootstrapping as it provides a good approximation of the population distribution.

title: Comparing Two Means
text: To compare the average trip distance on May $$1$$ with the average for all of $$2018$$, we can use bootstrapping to estimate the confidence interval for the difference between these two means.

title: Setting Up the Bootstrap
text: To perform bootstrapping, repeatedly resample the May $$1$$ dataset and calculate the mean trip distance for each resample. Then, compare these means to the overall mean for $$2018$$.
